senses.title: A natural inorganic solid
senses.titleCN: 矿物：天然产出的无机固体
senses.definition: a naturally formed inorganic solid with a definite chemical composition and a characteristic crystal structure
senses.definitionCN: 天然形成的无机固体，具有确定的化学成分与特征晶体结构
senses.example: Quartz is a mineral made of silicon and oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 石英是由硅与氧构成的矿物。
senses.why: Geology defines minerals by four tests at once: natural, inorganic, definite composition, ordered structure.
senses.whyCN: 地质学同时用四条标准界定矿物：天然、无机、成分确定、结构有序。

senses.title: Dietary minerals
senses.titleCN: 矿物质养分：人体必需的无机元素
senses.definition: in nutrition, the inorganic elements such as calcium, iron and zinc that the body needs in small amounts
senses.definitionCN: 营养学中指钙、铁、锌等人体少量必需的无机元素
senses.example: Leafy greens supply calcium and other minerals.
senses.exampleCN: 绿叶蔬菜提供钙与其他矿物质。
senses.why: Nutrition borrowed the geology word because these nutrients arrive as mineral salts rather than as carbon compounds.
senses.whyCN: 营养学借用地质学词汇，因为这些养分以矿物盐而非碳化合物的形式到来。

senses.title: Mineral water and springs
senses.titleCN: 矿泉水：含溶解矿物质的天然水
senses.definition: water drawn from a spring and containing dissolved mineral salts, often sold as a drink
senses.definitionCN: 取自泉水、含溶解矿物盐的水，常作为饮品出售
senses.example: The hotel serves local mineral water from the valley spring.
senses.exampleCN: 旅馆供应来自山谷泉眼的当地矿泉水。
senses.why: The adjective simply says what the water contains, and the phrase mineral water then became a product category.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是说明水含有什么，而「矿泉水」这一短语随后成了一个产品类别。

senses.title: Mineral resources and rights
senses.titleCN: 矿产资源与矿权：法律经济意义上的矿物
senses.definition: in law and economics, the valuable inorganic substances in the ground and the rights to extract them
senses.definitionCN: 法律与经济中指地下有价值的无机物质及开采它的权利
senses.example: The state owns all mineral rights beneath private land.
senses.exampleCN: 私有土地之下的一切矿权归国家所有。
senses.why: Because extraction is worth money, the word shifts from a scientific category to a legal asset.
senses.whyCN: 由于开采具有经济价值，这个词从科学分类转成了法律资产。

senses.title: Rock-forming minerals
senses.titleCN: 造岩矿物：组成岩石的基本单元
senses.definition: in petrology, the individual mineral species whose grains make up a rock
senses.definitionCN: 岩石学中指构成岩石颗粒的各个矿物种类
senses.example: Granite is a rock made of quartz, feldspar and mica minerals.
senses.exampleCN: 花岗岩是由石英、长石与云母等矿物构成的岩石。
senses.why: Petrologists must name the parts as well as the whole, so mineral is the countable unit inside an uncountable rock.
senses.whyCN: 岩石学家既要命名整体也要命名部件，因此 mineral 是岩石这个不可数整体中的可数单元。

senses.title: Ore minerals
senses.titleCN: 矿石矿物：值得开采提炼的矿物
senses.definition: the mineral in a deposit that contains a metal or other element valuable enough to extract
senses.definitionCN: 矿床中含金属或其他元素、值得提炼的矿物
senses.example: Chalcopyrite is the main ore mineral of copper.
senses.exampleCN: 黄铜矿是铜的主要矿石矿物。
senses.why: Mining distinguishes the valuable grains from the worthless gangue, so ore mineral is a commercial as well as a geological label.
senses.whyCN: 采矿把有价值的颗粒与无价值的脉石分开，因此矿石矿物既是地质标签也是商业标签。

senses.title: The mineral kingdom
senses.titleCN: 矿物界：旧自然分类中的第三界
senses.definition: in older natural history, the third division of the natural world beside the animal and vegetable kingdoms
senses.definitionCN: 旧自然史中指与动物界、植物界并列的自然界第三界
senses.example: Old textbooks divided nature into animal, vegetable and mineral kingdoms.
senses.exampleCN: 旧教科书把自然分为动物界、植物界与矿物界。
senses.why: Before modern chemistry, classifying by kingdom was the easiest way to place lifeless matter.
senses.whyCN: 在现代化学之前，按「界」分类是把无生命物质归位的最简便方法。

senses.title: Specimens and gems
senses.titleCN: 矿物标本与宝石：收藏与鉴赏对象
senses.definition: a cut or collected mineral specimen valued for colour, crystal form or rarity
senses.definitionCN: 因颜色、晶形或稀有性而被切磨或收藏的矿物标本
senses.example: The museum displays minerals from old copper mines.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出旧铜矿出产的矿物标本。
senses.why: Collectors treat the same scientific object as an aesthetic one, so the word also names what sits in a display case.
senses.whyCN: 收藏者把同一个科学对象当作审美对象，因此这个词也指展柜里的东西。

intro.en: Mineral comes from Medieval Latin minerale, from minera 'ore, mine'. The deeper origin of minera is disputed and may be Celtic.
intro.cn: mineral 出自中世纪拉丁 minerale，源自 minera「矿石、矿」。minera 的更深来源有争议，可能来自凯尔特语。

items.en: Medieval Latin minera meant 'ore, mine, pit'. It appears in mining and metallurgical texts from the late Middle Ages.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 minera 意为「矿石、矿、矿坑」，见于中世纪末的采矿与冶金文献。

items.en: Many etymologists link minera to a Celtic root for ore, seen in Welsh mwyn 'ore'. This link is generally accepted but not proved.
items.cn: 许多词源学家把 minera 与表示矿石的凯尔特词根联系起来，可见威尔士语 mwyn「矿石」。这一联系被普遍接受，但未经证实。

items.en: Others derive it from Latin minari 'to jut, to project', because ore bodies stand out from the rock. This explanation is less favoured.
items.cn: 另有人把它追溯到拉丁 minari「突出、伸出」，因为矿体在岩石中显眼。这一解释较少被采纳。

items.en: Old French mineral passed into English in the late Middle Ages, first as an adjective for substances dug from the earth.
items.cn: 古法语 mineral 在中世纪末进入英语，最初作形容词，指从地下挖出的物质。

items.en: Chemistry fixed the modern geological definition in the nineteenth century, and nutrition later borrowed the word for dietary elements.
items.cn: 化学在 19 世纪确立了现代地质学定义，营养学后来又借这个词指膳食元素。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the origin of minera is unresolved; both the Celtic and the Latin minari explanations are hypotheses, and the first English date is uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定：minera 的来源尚无定论；凯尔特说与拉丁 minari 说都属假说，英语首见年代亦存疑。

note.en: The first group holds words built on mineral that name studies or processes rather than the substance; the second holds earth materials that are often called minerals loosely.
note.cn: 第一组是由 mineral 构成、却指学科或过程的词；第二组是常被宽泛称作矿物的地球材料。

entries.definition: The scientific study of minerals, their composition, structure and classification. It is a discipline, not a substance.
entries.definitionCN: 研究矿物的成分、结构与分类的学科。它是一门学问，不是物质。

entries.definition: To convert organic matter into mineral form, or to impregnate something with minerals.
entries.definitionCN: 把有机物转化为矿物形态，或用矿物浸染某物。

entries.definition: Describes something that has been converted into or impregnated with mineral matter, such as mineralized bone.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已被转化为矿物或被矿物浸染的事物，如矿化骨。

entries.definition: A natural aggregate of one or more minerals. A rock is the whole mixture; a mineral is one ingredient.
entries.definitionCN: 由一种或多种矿物组成的天然集合体。岩石是整体混合物，矿物是其中一种成分。

entries.definition: A solid whose atoms are arranged in a repeating pattern. Many minerals form crystals, but glass is a solid without that order.
entries.definitionCN: 原子呈重复排列的固体。许多矿物形成晶体，但玻璃是缺乏这种有序性的固体。

entries.definition: Rock or mineral material rich enough in a metal to be mined at a profit. All ore contains minerals, but most minerals are not ore.
entries.definitionCN: 金属含量高到值得开采获利的岩石或矿物材料。矿石都含矿物，但多数矿物并非矿石。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: minera 'ore' + -ale: what comes out of a mine.
normal.cn: minera「矿石」+ -ale：从矿里出来的东西。

normal.en: The family runs mineralize, mineralization, mineralogy, mineralogist and mineralogical.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mineralize、mineralization、mineralogy、mineralogist、mineralogical。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: mineral water, mineral resources, mineral deposit, essential minerals.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：矿泉水、矿产资源、矿床、必需矿物质。

normal.en: A rock is a mixture; a mineral is one ingredient with a fixed formula.
normal.cn: 岩石是混合物；矿物是成分固定的一种配料。

normal.en: Nutrition calls calcium and iron minerals because they arrive as inorganic salts.
normal.cn: 营养学把钙与铁称为矿物质，因为它们以无机盐形式到来。

abstract.en: Picture a cut stone with flat shiny faces lying on a wooden tray.
abstract.cn: 想象一块切开的石头，平面闪亮，躺在木托盘上。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of still water with a faint mineral taste and a spring behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯静水，带一点矿物味，背后是一眼泉。

abstract.en: Picture an old chart dividing the world into animal, vegetable and mineral bands.
abstract.cn: 想象一张旧图把世界分成动物、植物与矿物三条带。

examples.en: The region is rich in mineral deposits but short of water.
examples.cn: 该地区矿产丰富，却缺水。

examples.en: Iron is a mineral that many people do not get enough of.
examples.cn: 铁是许多人摄入不足的一种矿物质。

examples.en: The geologist identified the green mineral as malachite.
examples.cn: 地质学家把那块绿色矿物鉴定为孔雀石。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mine（矿）+ ral」——从矿里挖出来的东西 → mineral 矿物

root: 中世纪拉丁 minera「矿石、矿」→ minerale → 古法语 mineral → 英语 mineral。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one substance from a crystal in rock to a nutrient in food, a product on a shelf, a legal right, an ore, an old kingdom and a museum specimen.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一种物质从岩石中的晶体走到食物里的养分、货架上的产品、法律上的权利、矿石、旧时的「界」与博物馆标本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a faceted stone on a tray beside a heap of white salt crystals.
core.cn: 核心意象：木托盘上的晶面矿石，旁边一小堆白色盐晶。

branches.en: GEOLOGY: the definition needs nature, no life, a fixed formula and an ordered structure.
branches.cn: 地质：定义需要天然、无生命、成分固定与结构有序四条。

branches.en: NUTRITION: the same word names the inorganic elements the body needs.
branches.cn: 营养：同一个词指身体所需的无机元素。

branches.en: PRODUCT: dissolved salts turn spring water into a branded drink.
branches.cn: 产品：溶解的盐把泉水变成有品牌的饮品。

branches.en: VALUE: rights underground and ore in the vein both measure the word in money.
branches.cn: 价值：地下的权利与矿脉中的矿石，都用钱来衡量这个词。

branches.en: CLASSIFICATION AND BEAUTY: an old kingdom and a display case are two ends of the same label.
branches.cn: 分类与美：旧时的「界」与展柜，是同一标签的两端。

intro.en: Mineral is a Medieval Latin noun ending in -ale, the suffix that turns a stem into a thing name, later used as an adjective without change.
intro.cn: mineral 是带 -ale 的中世纪拉丁名词，该后缀把词干变成事物名，后来它又原形用作形容词。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin minera supplied the stem and minerale the noun; the -alis ending later produced English mineralogy through a different path.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁 minera 提供词干、minerale 提供名词；-alis 词尾后来经另一条路径产生了英语 mineralogy。

items.meaning: a natural inorganic solid; also an adjective
items.meaningCN: 天然无机固体；也作形容词
items.example: The mineral is harder than steel.
Soil microbes mineralize the organic matter.
items.exampleCN: 土壤微生物把有机质矿化。
矿化作用保存了这具化石。
矿物学按对称性给晶体分类。
矿物学家鉴定了这块标本。

items.example: The mineralogical survey mapped the district.
items.exampleCN: 矿物学调查绘制了该区地图。

items.meaning: to remove minerals from water or bone
items.meaningCN: 从水或骨中去除矿物质
items.example: The filter demineralizes the tap water.
items.exampleCN: 该过滤器去除自来水中的矿物质。

items.meaning: a person who works in a mine
items.example: The miners went down at dawn.

latinEntries.structure: minera, minerae (f., Medieval Latin, first declension)

latinEntries.meaning: a thing dug from the earth

definition_zh: 最小值；最低限度；最低点；极小值；最小的；最低的
definition_en: the smallest amount, level or point that is possible, allowed or reached, or the lowest value of a set or function
core_image: 量筒底部划着一道红线，任何水位都不能低于它
scene: 清晨的水库边，管理员看着水位尺上那道浅浅的红线，提醒同伴抽水不能低于这里。The reservoir is kept at a minimum during the dry months.
sceneCN: 这里 minimum 是「最低水位、最低限度」（第 1 个义项：可能或允许的最小量）；句意为干旱月份水库水位被维持在最低限度。画面里可抓住的物件：水位尺、红线、抽水泵。

pos.zh: 最小值；最低限度；最低点；极小值

collocations.zh: 把某事物控制在最低限度

senses.title: The smallest possible amount
senses.definition: the smallest amount of something that is possible, needed or allowed
senses.definitionCN: 某事物可能、需要或被允许的最小数量
senses.example: Keep the noise to a minimum after ten.
senses.exampleCN: 十点以后把噪音降到最低。
senses.why: Latin minimum is the neuter form of minimus, the smallest, and it entered English as a noun for the least quantity that can be reached or permitted.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 minimum 是 minimus（最小的）的中性形式，进入英语时就是一个名词，指能够达到或被允许的最小数量。

senses.title: The lowest point reached
senses.definition: the lowest level or point that a changing quantity falls to before it rises again
senses.definitionCN: 某个变化中的量在下落之后、回升之前所到的最低水平或位置
senses.example: The river reaches its minimum in late summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河在夏末降到最低水位。
senses.why: Anything that rises and falls traces a curve, and the bottom of that curve is naturally called its minimum; the word moves from an allowed limit to an observed low.
senses.whyCN: 凡是有起伏的东西都会画出曲线，曲线的最低处自然被叫作 minimum；词义于是从「被允许的下限」转到「观察到的低点」。

senses.title: Lowest allowed by a rule
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean the smallest or lowest that a rule, price or standard permits
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，指规则、价格或标准所允许的最小或最低值
senses.example: The minimum age for driving is eighteen in many countries.
senses.exampleCN: 许多国家的驾车最低年龄是十八岁。
senses.why: English turns the noun into a modifier by placing it before another noun; minimum wage is the wage at the bottom of the permitted scale, with no ending added.
senses.whyCN: 英语把名词放到另一个名词前面就使它成为修饰语；minimum wage 就是允许范围最底端的工资，词形不加任何词尾。

senses.title: The lowest value of a set or function
senses.definition: the smallest value that a set of numbers or a mathematical function takes
senses.definitionCN: 一组数值或一个数学函数所能取到的最小值
senses.example: The curve has a minimum at the centre and rises on both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 这条曲线在中央有极小值，两侧向上升高。
senses.why: Mathematics needed a precise name for the bottom of a graph, and it borrowed the Latin word unchanged; the everyday sense of a lower bound became a technical term.
senses.whyCN: 数学需要给图像的最低处一个精确的名字，于是原封不动地借用了这个拉丁词；日常的「下界」义由此变成了术语。

intro.en: Minimum came straight from Latin, where it was the neuter form of the word for smallest; English borrowed it in the seventeenth century as a noun for the least amount.
intro.cn: minimum 直接来自拉丁语，是「最小的」一词的中性形式；英语在十七世纪把它借来，作名词指最小量。

items.en: Parvus meant small; its comparative minor and superlative minimus are generally treated as suppletive forms, borrowed from a related root rather than built with a regular ending.
items.cn: parvus 意为「小的」；一般认为它的比较级 minor 与最高级 minimus 属于补充式形式，借自相关词根，而不是用规则词尾构成。

items.en: Minimus meant the smallest or least, and it supplied the top of the scale in phrases such as minimus natu, the youngest.
items.cn: minimus 意为最小的、最少的；在 minimus natu（最年幼者）这类说法里，它标出等级序列的最末端。

items.en: The neuter singular minimum was used as a noun for the smallest amount, and this exact form was taken over by English.
items.cn: 中性单数形式 minimum 被当作名词使用，指最小量；英语原样借用的正是这个形式。

items.en: Writers borrowed minimum in the seventeenth century, first in scientific and mathematical writing where a precise lower bound was needed.
items.cn: 十七世纪的作者借入 minimum，最早用在科学与数学写作中，因为那里需要一个精确的下界。

items.en: Modern English uses it as a noun and as a modifier, and keeps the Latin plural minima beside the English minimums.
items.cn: 现代英语让它作名词也作修饰语，并在英语复数 minimums 之外保留拉丁式复数 minima。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the Latin comparison of small; the near-meaning group collects other words for the least amount or the bottom of a scale.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁「小」的比较之上的形式；近义组收其他表示最小量或标度底端的词。

entries.definition: As small as possible; barely enough to count.
entries.definitionCN: 尽可能小的；刚刚够得上数的。

entries.definition: To reduce something to the smallest possible amount or level.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事物减到尽可能小的数量或程度。

entries.definition: Smaller, less important, or not yet legally adult; it belongs to the same Latin comparison of small.
entries.definitionCN: 较小的、较次要的，或尚未成年的；它属于同一个拉丁「小」的比较系列。

entries.definition: A tiny amount, or a short note value in early music.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的量，或早期音乐中短小的音符时值。

entries.definition: The smallest amount or degree of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物最小的数量或程度。

entries.definition: The lowest level that prices or amounts are allowed to reach.
entries.definitionCN: 价格或数量被允许降到的最低水平。

entries.definition: The lowest point of something, especially of a changing situation.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物的最低点，尤指变化中的境况。

entries.definition: The lowest part or level of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的最下部或最低水平。

normalIntro.en: Minimum is the superlative of a Latin word for small, and its family keeps circling the idea of the least amount or the bottom of a scale.
normalIntro.cn: minimum 是拉丁语「小」一词的最高级形式，它的一族词始终围着「最小量」或「标度底端」打转。

normal.en: Minimus is Latin for smallest, and minimum is its neuter form, so the word already carries the comparison inside it.
normal.cn: minimus 是拉丁语「最小的」，minimum 是它的中性形式，所以这个词本身就带着比较。

normal.en: The min- root recurs in minor, minus and minute: all of them measure something smaller or less.
normal.cn: min- 这个词根反复出现在 minor、minus 与 minute 里：它们都在度量更小或更少的东西。

normal.en: Keep something to a minimum is the everyday frame: whatever follows is the thing you want as small as possible.
normal.cn: keep something to a minimum 是日常框架：后面接的东西，就是你希望尽量压小的对象。

normal.en: Minimum wage and minimum age show the word acting as a modifier without any added ending.
normal.cn: minimum wage 与 minimum age 展示了这个词不靠任何词尾就充当修饰语。

normal.en: Maximum is its opposite, built with the Latin superlative for great, so the pair mark the two ends of a scale.
normal.cn: maximum 是它的反面，用拉丁语表示「大」的最高级构成；这一对词标出一段标度的两端。

abstract.en: Picture a red line near the floor of a measuring tube: everything must stay above it.
abstract.cn: 想象量筒底部附近有一道红线，所有东西都必须停在它上面。

abstract.en: A minimum is not zero; it is the lowest point that still counts as acceptable.
abstract.cn: minimum 并不是零，而是仍然算得上合格的最低点。

abstract.en: Every curve that dips has a floor, and English uses one Latin word for that floor.
abstract.cn: 每条下探的曲线都有一个底，英语用一个拉丁词来指这个底。

examples.en: Keep the noise to a minimum after ten.
examples.cn: 十点以后把噪音降到最低。

examples.en: The river reaches its minimum in late summer.
examples.cn: 这条河在夏末降到最低水位。

examples.en: The minimum age for driving is eighteen in many countries.
examples.cn: 许多国家的驾车最低年龄是十八岁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迷你闷」——空间小得人一进去就发闷，小到不能再小；minimum 是最小值、最低限度。

root: 拉丁语 minimus（最小的）是 parvus（小）的最高级形式；中性形式 minimum 被英语原样借作名词「最小量」。一般认为 minimus 与 minus（较少）、minuere（减少）同属一个词根。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the least amount; the senses run from an allowed lower limit to an observed low, then to attributive and mathematical uses.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是最小量；各义项从被允许的下限，走到观察到的低点，再延伸到定语用法与数学术语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red line near the bottom of a measuring tube, marking the lowest level allowed.
core.cn: 核心意象：量筒底部附近的一道红线，标出允许的最低水位。

branches.en: a red line that the water must not drop below
branches.cn: 水位不得低于的那道红线

branches.en: a river shrinking to its shallowest week
branches.cn: 河水缩到最浅的那一周

branches.en: a sign at the gate stating the youngest age allowed
branches.cn: 门口写明最低年龄的牌子

branches.en: a curve dipping to a single low point
branches.cn: 曲线下探到唯一的最低点

branches.en: a rulebook with its floor printed in bold
branches.cn: 把下限印得又粗又醒目的规章

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin superlative for small, and its family spreads across adjectives, verbs and nouns about making things less.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示「小」的最高级构成，它的一族词散落在形容词、动词与名词里，都与「使之更少」有关。

latinIntro.en: Minimum is the neuter form of the Latin superlative for small, and the same root runs through minor, minus and minimize.
latinIntro.cn: minimum 是拉丁语「最小」最高级的中性形式，同一词根贯穿 minor、minus 与 minimize。

definition_zh: 部长；大臣；牧师；公使
definition_en: a senior member of a government who heads a department, a religious leader who leads worship, or a diplomat ranked below an ambassador
core_image: 一个身着礼服的人站在门口，手里捧着别人交办的文件
scene: 议会走廊里，记者们围住一位刚走出会议室的人，等他开口谈预算。The minister answered questions for nearly an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 minister 是「部长」（第 1 个义项：主管政府部门的资深政客）；句意为部长回答了将近一小时的提问。画面里可抓住的物件：议会走廊、会议室门、录音笔。

derivatives.zh: 由 minister 加 -ial 构成，义为「部长的；大臣的；牧师的」
由 minister 加 -y 构成，义为「部；内阁部门；神职」
由拉丁 ministrare 加 -ation 构成，义为「服侍；宗教仪式」
由拉丁 ad- 加 ministrare 构成，义为「管理；施行」

senses.title: A head of a government department
senses.definition: a senior politician who is in charge of a government department
senses.definitionCN: 主管某一个政府部门的资深政界人物
senses.example: The finance minister resigned after the budget vote.
senses.exampleCN: 预算表决之后，财政部长辞职了。
senses.why: Latin minister first meant a servant or attendant; a person who served the crown at the head of an office grew into the modern sense of a senior state official.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 minister 最初指仆人、随从；在朝廷里替君主办事、主管一个衙门的人，逐渐长成现代「政府部长」的意思。

senses.title: A religious leader of a congregation
senses.definition: a person ordained to lead worship and care for a congregation, especially in Protestant churches
senses.definitionCN: 受按立以主持礼拜、照看会众的人，尤指新教教会的牧师
senses.example: The minister read the names of the dead aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 牧师大声念出逝者的名字。
senses.why: The same word for a servant was used in the church for one who serves the congregation; the religious sense is older in English than the political one.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示「仆人」的词在教会里指服侍会众的人；在英语里，宗教义比政治义出现得更早。

senses.title: A diplomat below an ambassador
senses.definition: a diplomatic representative of a country, ranking below an ambassador and above lower embassy staff
senses.definitionCN: 一国派出的外交代表，地位低于大使、高于使馆较低级别的职员
senses.example: She was posted to the embassy as minister for trade.
senses.exampleCN: 她被派往使馆担任贸易公使。
senses.why: Diplomacy borrowed the ranking vocabulary of courts: a minister served a sovereign abroad, and the title stayed for envoys who rank just under an ambassador.
senses.whyCN: 外交沿用宫廷的等级词汇：minister 曾在国外替君主办事，这个头衔便留给地位略低于大使的使节。

intro.en: Minister goes back to a Latin word for a servant, and its journey from household attendant to cabinet member and clergy explains why one word covers three jobs.
intro.cn: minister 可追到拉丁语中表示仆人的词；它从家仆走到内阁成员与神职人员，这条路径解释了一个词为何能涵盖三种职务。

items.en: Minus meant less, and from it Latin built words for people or things that stood lower in a hierarchy.
items.cn: minus 意为较少、较低；拉丁语由它造出表示在等级中位置较低的人或事物的词。

items.en: Minister named an attendant, a servant or an agent who acted for someone else, including an assistant in religious rites.
items.cn: minister 指随从、仆人或替别人办事的代理人，也包括宗教仪式中的助手。

items.en: The verb ministrare meant to serve, to attend or to manage, and it produced a whole family of English words such as administer.
items.cn: 动词 ministrare 意为服侍、随侍或经办，由此产生 administer 等一整族英语词。

items.en: Old French took the noun as menistre, a servant or an official, and carried it into English after the Norman conquest.
items.cn: 古法语把名词写作 menistre，指仆人或官员，诺曼征服之后传入英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps minister for a cabinet member, a clergyperson and a mid-ranked diplomat, while ministry splits off as the office itself.
items.cn: 现代英语用 minister 指内阁成员、神职人员与中等层级的外交官，而 ministry 则分出去指职务机构本身。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the same Latin stem of service; the near-meaning group collects other titles for officials, clergy and envoys.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「服务」词干上的词；近义组收官员、神职人员与使节的其他称谓。

entries.definition: A government department, the cabinet, or the office of a religious minister.
entries.definitionCN: 政府部门、内阁，或牧师的职务。

entries.definition: Relating to a minister, a government department or a pastor's duties.
entries.definitionCN: 与部长、政府部门或牧师职责有关的。

entries.definition: To manage an organization or to give a treatment or a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 管理一个机构，或施行某种治疗、执行某项规则。

entries.definition: The act of serving or helping, often in a religious setting.
entries.definitionCN: 服侍、帮助的行为，常用于宗教场合。

entries.definition: A senior government official who heads a department in the United States.
entries.definitionCN: 美国联邦政府中主管一个部门的资深官员。

entries.definition: A minister in charge of a church and its congregation.
entries.definitionCN: 主管一间教堂及其会众的牧师。

entries.definition: A diplomat sent to represent a country, usually ranking below an ambassador.
entries.definitionCN: 被派往代表一国的外交官，通常地位低于大使。

entries.definition: A person who holds a position of authority in a government or organization.
entries.definitionCN: 在政府或机构中担任有权威职位的人。

normalIntro.en: The word began as Latin for a servant, and every modern sense still keeps a trace of someone acting on another's behalf.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初是拉丁语中的「仆人」，每个现代义项都还留着「替别人办事」的痕迹。

normal.en: Latin minister meant servant or attendant, which is why the word fits both a cabinet member serving the state and a pastor serving a congregation.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 minister 意为仆人或随从，所以这个词既适合替国家办事的内阁成员，也适合服侍会众的牧师。

normal.en: Ministrare is the verb behind administer, so minister and administer are siblings rather than unrelated words.
normal.cn: ministrare 是 administer 背后的动词，所以 minister 与 administer 是同胞词，而非互不相干的词。

normal.en: Ministry is the office, minister is the person: the -y ending names the institution, the bare word names the human being.
normal.cn: ministry 是机构，minister 是人：-y 词尾命名制度，光秃秃的词干则指具体的人。

normal.en: Prime minister is a fixed phrase, and the stress falls on the first word, so it sounds like one title rather than two.
normal.cn: prime minister 是固定说法，重音落在第一个词上，所以听起来像一个头衔而不是两个词。

normal.en: The diplomatic rank is the oldest of the three modern uses in court language, because an envoy was literally a servant sent abroad.
normal.cn: 三个现代义项里，外交级别在宫廷用语中出现得最早，因为使节字面上就是被派往国外的仆人。

abstract.en: Picture a servant holding a sealed letter at a palace door: the same figure becomes a cabinet member and a pastor.
abstract.cn: 想象一个仆人站在宫门口，手里拿着一封封好的信：同一个人物后来变成了内阁成员与牧师。

abstract.en: A minister never acts alone; the word always points to someone who works for another party.
abstract.cn: minister 从不单独行动；这个词始终指向替另一方办事的人。

abstract.en: One Latin noun for service splits into a person, an office and a rank, like a single trunk with three branches.
abstract.cn: 一个表示服务的拉丁名词分成一个人、一个机构与一个级别，像一根主干长出三根枝条。

examples.en: The finance minister resigned after the budget vote.
examples.cn: 预算表决之后，财政部长辞职了。

examples.en: The minister read the names of the dead aloud.
examples.cn: 牧师大声念出逝者的名字。

examples.en: She was posted to the embassy as minister for trade.
examples.cn: 她被派往使馆担任贸易公使。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迷你斯特」——听上去像「迷你」的随从，职位再高也是替国家办事的仆从；minister 是部长、大臣。

root: 拉丁语 minister（仆人、随从）一般认为由 minus（较少、较低）加比较级后缀构成，义为「地位较低者」；动词 ministrare（服侍、经办）派生 administer 等词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is service on behalf of another; the senses divide into the head of a department, the leader of a congregation, and a diplomatic rank.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是替他人服务；各义项分成主管部门的首长、会众的属灵领袖，以及一个外交级别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a servant in formal dress standing at a door, holding papers handed over by someone else.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个穿礼服的仆人站在门口，手里捧着别人交办的文件。

branches.en: a politician leaving a cabinet room under a wall of cameras
branches.cn: 在镜头包围下走出内阁会议室的政客

branches.en: a pastor reading names from a pulpit
branches.cn: 在讲坛上念名字的牧师

branches.en: an envoy handing over papers in a foreign capital
branches.cn: 在异国首都递交文件的使节

branches.en: one title shared by a cabinet post and a diplomatic rank
branches.cn: 同一个头衔既指内阁职位又指外交级别

branches.en: a figure who speaks for a community abroad or before a congregation
branches.cn: 在海外或会众面前代表群体说话的人

intro.en: Minister is a Latin noun of service, backed by a verb of serving and by the suffix that turns it into an office.
intro.cn: minister 是表示服务的拉丁名词，背后有一个表示服侍的动词，以及把它变成机构名的后缀。

latinIntro.en: The word is a Latin noun of service, and the same stem reappears in ministry, administer and ministerial.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是表示「服务」的拉丁名词，同一词干又出现在 ministry、administer 与 ministerial 中。

definition_zh: 部；内阁部门；内阁；执政期；牧师职务；神职
definition_en: a government department headed by a minister, the government as a whole, or the office and work of a religious minister
core_image: 一栋办公楼的门旁挂着铜牌，牌上只刻一个部门的名字
scene: 教堂旁边的办公楼里，工作人员把一份新规定贴上公告栏，纸角压着一个部门印章。The ministry published the new rules on its website.
sceneCN: 这里 ministry 是「政府部门、部」（第 1 个义项：由部长主管的政府机关）；句意为该部门在网站上公布了新规定。画面里可抓住的物件：公告栏、部门印章、办公楼铜牌。

pos.zh: 部；内阁部门；内阁；执政期；牧师职务；神职

derivatives.zh: 与 ministry 同一词干，指担任职务的人，义为「部长；大臣；牧师」
由 minister 加 -ial 构成，义为「部长的；内阁的；牧师的」
由拉丁 ministrare 加 -ant 构成，指「服侍者；主持仪式的」
由拉丁 administrare 加 -ation 构成，义为「管理；行政」

senses.title: A government department
senses.definition: a department of government led by a minister and responsible for one area of public life
senses.definitionCN: 由部长领导、负责某一方面公共事务的政府部门
senses.example: The Ministry of Health issued new guidance on masks.
senses.exampleCN: 卫生部发布了关于口罩的新指引。
senses.why: Latin ministerium meant service or office; when a minister took charge of an area of public service, the office itself came to be called a ministry.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ministerium 意为「服务、职务」；当部长主管某一方面的公共事务时，那个职务机构本身就被称为 ministry。

senses.title: The government or its term in office
senses.definition: a government led by a prime minister, or the period during which it holds power
senses.definitionCN: 由总理或首相领导的一届政府，或它掌权的时期
senses.example: The ministry fell after losing a vote of confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 内阁在失去信任投票后倒台。
senses.why: Because a ministry is the whole set of ministers serving together, the word shifted from one department to the cabinet and to the time it stays in power.
senses.whyCN: 因为 ministry 也指共同任职的一整批部长，词义便从一个部门转到整个内阁，再转到它掌权的时期。

senses.title: The office of a religious minister
senses.definition: the profession or work of an ordained religious minister, or the clergy as a body
senses.definitionCN: 受按立牧师的职业与工作，或作为整体的神职人员
senses.example: She left teaching to enter the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 她离开教职，进入神职。
senses.why: The same Latin word for service was applied to the church, where ministry names the work of serving a congregation rather than a government office.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示「服务」的拉丁词也被用到教会，这里的 ministry 指服侍会众的工作，而不是政府机关。

intro.en: Ministry is the office built on the Latin noun for service, and English uses it for both a government department and the work of the church.
intro.cn: ministry 是建立在拉丁语「服务」名词之上的职务，英语用它兼指政府部门与教会工作。

items.en: Minister meant a servant or attendant, and everything built on it keeps the idea of service.
items.cn: minister 指仆人或随从，凡由它构成的词都保留了「服务」的观念。

items.en: Ministerium named service, office or function, and it is the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: ministerium 指服务、职务或职能，是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French carried the word as menistere, meaning office or service, before it passed into English.
items.cn: 古法语把它写作 menistere，意为职务或服务，随后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English ministry covered service and the work of the clergy, and the political sense joined it later.
items.cn: 中古英语的 ministry 覆盖服务与神职工作，政治义后来才加入。

items.en: Modern English uses ministry for a department of state, for a whole government, and for the religious vocation.
items.cn: 现代英语用 ministry 指国家部门、整个内阁，以及宗教使命。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem of service and management; the near-meaning group collects names for departments, cabinets and clergy.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁「服务、管理」词干上的词；近义组收部门、内阁与神职人员的名称。

entries.definition: The person who heads a department or leads a congregation.
entries.definitionCN: 主管一个部门或带领会众的人。

entries.definition: Relating to a minister or to a government department.
entries.definitionCN: 与部长或政府部门有关的。

entries.definition: To manage affairs or to put a rule or treatment into effect.
entries.definitionCN: 管理事务，或施行某项规则、治疗。

entries.definition: The act of serving or assisting, especially in worship.
entries.definitionCN: 服侍或协助的行为，尤指在礼拜中。

entries.definition: A division of a government or a large organization.
entries.definitionCN: 政府或大型机构中的一个部门。

entries.definition: The group of senior ministers who advise a prime minister or president.
entries.definitionCN: 为首相或总统提供建议的一批高级部长。

entries.definition: The body of ordained religious leaders.
entries.definitionCN: 受按立的宗教领袖全体。

entries.definition: A government office or a division of one.
entries.definitionCN: 政府机关或其中的一个部门。

normalIntro.en: Ministry is the office that grows out of a minister's service, and the family keeps the same Latin stem in view.
normalIntro.cn: ministry 是从 minister 的服务中长出来的职务机构，整族词都共用同一个拉丁词干。

normal.en: Ministry is built on minister, the person; the -y ending turns the servant into the office he or she holds.
normal.cn: ministry 建立在 minister 这个「人」之上；-y 词尾把仆人变成他所担任的职务。

normal.en: Latin ministerium meant service or function, so ministry is literally the job rather than the building.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 ministerium 意为服务或职能，所以 ministry 字面上是那份工作，而不是那栋楼。

normal.en: Ministry of Education, foreign ministry and ministry of defence all show the word naming a branch of government.
normal.cn: Ministry of Education、foreign ministry 与 ministry of defence 都展示了这个词如何命名政府的一个分支。

normal.en: Enter the ministry is a fixed phrase for becoming an ordained minister, where the word means vocation rather than department.
normal.cn: enter the ministry 是成为按立牧师的固定说法，这里的词义是使命而非部门。

normal.en: Administration and administer share the same ministrare root, so the whole family is about handling affairs for someone else.
normal.cn: administration 与 administer 共用 ministrare 这个词根，所以整族词都与替别人经办事务有关。

abstract.en: Picture a brass plate on a door: one word names the people inside, the work they do and the time they hold office.
abstract.cn: 想象门上一块铜牌：一个词同时说出里面的人、他们做的事，以及他们任职的时间。

abstract.en: A ministry is a service organized into an office, whether the service is to the state or to a congregation.
abstract.cn: ministry 是被组织成机构的服务，无论对象是国家还是会众。

abstract.en: One Latin noun for service grows into a department, a cabinet and a calling without changing its stem.
abstract.cn: 一个表示服务的拉丁名词长成部门、内阁与使命，词干始终没变。

examples.en: The Ministry of Health issued new guidance on masks.

examples.en: The ministry fell after losing a vote of confidence.
examples.cn: 内阁在失去信任投票后倒台。

examples.en: She left teaching to enter the ministry.
examples.cn: 她离开教职，进入神职。

root: 拉丁语 ministerium（服务、职务）源自 minister（仆人、随从）；经古法语进入英语，先指服侍与神职，后指政府部门与内阁。

sensesIntro.en: The core is service organized as an office; the senses run from a single department to the whole cabinet and to the religious vocation.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被组织成机构的服务；各义项从单个部门走到整个内阁，再到宗教使命。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brass nameplate on a government building, with one department's name and a seal beneath it.
core.cn: 核心意象：政府大楼门旁的铜牌，刻着一个部门的名字，下面压着印章。

branches.cn: 部门门口只刻一个部门名的铜牌

branches.en: ministers seated around a cabinet table
branches.cn: 围坐内阁桌旁的一排部长

branches.en: a young pastor being ordained before a congregation
branches.cn: 在会众面前受按立的年轻牧师

branches.en: a department that speaks for the whole government
branches.cn: 代表整个政府发声的部门

branches.en: one word holding both a political term and a calling

intro.en: Ministry is the office formed from the Latin noun for service, and its items trace how a job becomes an institution.

scene: 报告里列了三处小错，但没有改变结论。The report listed three minor errors, none of which changed the conclusion.
sceneCN: 这里 minor 是「轻微的、不严重的」（第 3 个义项：程度轻、不严重）；句意：报告列出三处轻微错误，没有一处改变结论。场景要点：一份校样上三处小小的红笔改动、旁边依然通过的结论页、天平上微微上翘的一端；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 较小的；次要的；轻微的；未成年的；（音乐）小调的
未成年人；辅修科目；（逻辑）小前提

forms.label: 名词复数（形容词无比较级形式）

derivatives.zh: 少数；少数派；未成年状态
少数派的；少数族群的（作定语）

senses.title: The smaller of two things
senses.definition: smaller in size, extent, or number when compared with a paired thing
senses.definitionCN: 与配对的事物相比，在尺寸、范围或数量上更小
senses.example: The minor axis of the ellipse is the shorter one.
senses.exampleCN: 椭圆的短轴就是较短的那条轴。
senses.why: Latin minor is a comparative, 'smaller'. It does not mean small in general but smaller than the other member of a pair, which is why the word so often appears beside major.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 minor 是比较级，意为“更小的”。它不是泛泛地表示小，而是比同一对里的另一个更小，因此这个词常与 major 并出现。

senses.title: Less important: a secondary part
senses.definition: less important, powerful, or influential than the main person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 不如主要的人或事物重要、有力量或有影响
senses.example: He played a minor role in the negotiations.
senses.exampleCN: 他在谈判中只起了次要作用。
senses.why: Rank is treated as weight on a balance. The lighter pan rises, and whatever sits there is minor: present, but not carrying the decision.
senses.whyCN: 等级被当成天平上的重量。较轻的那一端会翘起，放在那一端的东西就是 minor：它在场，却不承担决定。

senses.title: Slight: not serious
senses.definition: small enough in degree to be unimportant or easy to deal with
senses.definitionCN: 程度小到无关紧要或容易处理
senses.example: She suffered only minor injuries in the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 她在撞车中只受了轻伤。
senses.why: The comparison has faded and only the smallness remains. A minor injury is not measured against a major one; it is simply below the threshold of seriousness.
senses.whyCN: 比较对象已经淡去，只剩下“小”。轻伤并不是拿来与重伤对比，它只是落在“严重”这道门槛之下。

senses.title: Underage: below the legal age
senses.titleCN: 未成年的：低于法定年龄
senses.definition: not yet old enough to have full legal rights or responsibilities
senses.definitionCN: 年龄尚不足以拥有完整法律权利或承担责任
senses.example: Minor children must be accompanied by an adult.
senses.exampleCN: 未成年子女必须由成年人陪同。
senses.why: Age is another scale, and the legal threshold is the line between full and lesser status. A person below that line is minor in the eyes of the law.
senses.whyCN: 年龄是另一把尺子，法定门槛就是完整身份与次一等身份之间的界线。线以下的人在法律眼里就是 minor。

senses.title: Music: a minor key or interval
senses.definition: in music, belonging to a key or interval built on a minor third, shorter than the corresponding major one
senses.definitionCN: 在音乐中，属于以小三度构成的小调或音程，比对应的大调或大音程更短
senses.example: The second movement slips into a minor key.
senses.exampleCN: 第二乐章转入了小调。
senses.why: The interval is literally lesser: a minor third is shorter than the major third. The word keeps its comparative sense inside music theory.
senses.whyCN: 这个音程字面上就是“较小的”：小三度比大三度短。这个词在乐理内部保留了它的比较级含义。

senses.title: Sports: the minor leagues
senses.definition: in sport, the leagues or competitions below the top professional level
senses.definitionCN: 体育中低于顶级职业水平的联赛或赛事
senses.example: He spent four seasons in the minor leagues before being called up.
senses.exampleCN: 他在小联盟打了四个赛季才被上调。
senses.why: The league table is a ranking, and the minor leagues sit one step below the major ones. The word marks position on that ladder, not the size of the players.
senses.whyCN: 联赛表就是一张排名，小联盟坐在大联盟下面一级。这个词标记的是梯子上的位置，而不是球员的体型。

senses.title: Logic: the minor premise
senses.definition: in a syllogism, the premise that contains the subject of the conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 在三段论中，包含结论主项的那个前提
senses.example: The minor premise says that Socrates is a man.
senses.exampleCN: 小前提说苏格拉底是人。
senses.why: A syllogism has a greater and a lesser premise. The one carrying the subject is the lesser member of the pair, so it inherited the name minor.
senses.whyCN: 三段论有一个大前提和一个小前提。承载主项的那一个是这对命题中较小的一员，于是继承了 minor 这个名字。

senses.title: Academic: a secondary subject
senses.definition: a subject studied at university in addition to the main subject, with fewer credits
senses.definitionCN: 在大学里除主修之外学习的科目，所需学分较少
senses.example: She chose history as her minor.
senses.exampleCN: 她选择了历史作为辅修。
senses.why: The degree has a major and a minor: the second subject carries less weight in the total. It is the academic version of the lighter pan.
senses.whyCN: 学位有一个主修和一个辅修：第二门科目在总量里分量更轻。它就是天平上较轻那一端的学业版本。

senses.title: A person below legal age
senses.definition: a person who has not reached the age at which the law grants full adult rights
senses.definitionCN: 尚未达到法律授予完整成年人权利的年龄的人
senses.example: The club is not allowed to sell alcohol to minors.
senses.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部不得向未成年人售酒。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun by leaving out the person: 'a minor person' shortened to 'a minor'. Legal writing uses it as a stable category.
senses.whyCN: 形容词省略了所修饰的人，变成了名词：“一个未成年的人”缩成“一个未成年人”。法律文本把它用作固定类别。

intro.en: Minor is a Latin comparative borrowed whole, first through the Franciscans and then in general use. Its relation to parvus is grammatical rather than root-based, and that point is disputed in the sources.
intro.cn: minor 是整体借入的拉丁语比较级，先经方济各会进入英语，再进入一般用法。它与 parvus 的关系是语法性的而非词根性的，这一点在资料中存在争议。

items.en: First recorded in English in frere menour 'Franciscan friar', literally 'minor friar', from Latin minor. The order's founder chose Fratres Minores, 'lesser brethren', for humility.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 13 世纪早期，出现在 frere menour“方济各会修士”中，字面是“较小的修士”，来自拉丁语 minor。该会创始人选用 Fratres Minores“小兄弟会”，是出于谦卑。

items.en: Latin minor meant 'less, lesser, smaller, junior', figuratively 'inferior, less important'. It was formed as the masculine/feminine of minus on the mistaken assumption that minus was a neuter comparative. Latin grammars traditionally pair parvus 'small' with minor and minimus, but the roots differ: minor belongs to *mei-, while parvus has a separate origin, itself not fully settled. The pairing is suppletive, grammatical rather than etymological, and its root relation is disputed.
items.cn: 拉丁语 minor 意为“更少、更小、更年幼”，引申为“较低、较不重要”。它是把 minus 误当作中性比较级之后，按阳性／阴性形式造出来的。拉丁语法传统把 parvus“小”与 minor、minimus 配成一组比较级和最高级，但两者词根不同：minor 属于 *mei-，parvus 另有来源，其自身来源也未完全定论。这种配对是异根补充式，属于语法配对而非词源配对，其词根关联存在争议。

items.en: The family goes back to PIE *mei- (2) 'small', the root also behind minus, minimum, diminish, minute and minuscule.
items.cn: 这个词族可追溯到原始印欧语 *mei-（第二支）“小”，该词根也是 minus、minimum、diminish、minute、minuscule 的来源。

items.en: The general adjectival sense 'lesser or smaller than the other' is recorded from early 15c.; 'underage' is recorded from the 1570s.
items.cn: 一般形容词义“比另一个更小、更次要”于 15 世纪早期有记录；“未成年的”义于 16 世纪 70 年代有记录。

items.en: From the 1610s the noun means 'a person below legal age'. The musical sense dates from the 1690s, for intervals and keys built on a minor third; chords follow by 1797.
items.cn: 名词从 17 世纪 10 年代起表示“未达法定年龄的人”。音乐义始于 17 世纪 90 年代，指以小三度构成的音程与调；和弦用法到 1797 年才出现。

items.en: Minor league is recorded from 1884, with the figurative extension by 1926. The academic minor is from 1890, and the verb 'to minor in' from 1905.
items.cn: minor league 于 1884 年有记录，其比喻用法到 1926 年出现。学业上的“辅修”始于 1890 年，动词用法“辅修”始于 1905 年。

note.en: The first group separates the sound-alike miner, the derived noun minority and the superlative neighbour minimum. The second group compares minor with small, lesser, its opposite major, and slight.
note.cn: 第一组区分同音的 miner、派生名词 minority 和最高级邻词 minimum；第二组把 minor 与 small、lesser、它的反义 major 以及 slight 作比较。

entries.definition: a person who works in a mine. It sounds almost the same as minor but comes from mine, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 在矿里工作的人。它与 minor 读音几乎相同，却来自 mine 这条不同的词根。

entries.definition: a smaller group, or the state of being under legal age. It is the noun built on minor, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 少数群体，或未成年状态。它是建立在 minor 之上的名词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: the smallest amount possible. It comes from minimus, the superlative that sits above minor on the same Latin scale.
entries.definitionCN: 可能的最小量。它来自 minimus，即同一把拉丁尺子上高于 minor 的最高级。

entries.definition: a musical key built on a minor third. It is a fixed compound using the adjective, not a separate root word or a legal term.
entries.definitionCN: 以小三级构成的小调。它是使用这个形容词的固定复合词，不是另一个词根词，也不是法律用语。

entries.definition: little in size or amount. It is a plain description with no comparison built in, while minor always implies a partner it is measured against.
entries.definitionCN: 尺寸或数量小。它是没有内置比较的平实描述，而 minor 总暗示着一个被拿来对照的伙伴。

entries.definition: smaller in importance or degree. It is a formal comparative close to minor, but it cannot mean 'underage' or name a musical key.
entries.definitionCN: 在重要性或程度上更小。它是接近 minor 的正式比较级，但不能表示“未成年”，也不能指音乐调性。

entries.definition: greater or more important. It is the direct opposite of minor in rank, in music, in sport and in academic study.
entries.definitionCN: 更大的；更重要的。它在等级、音乐、体育和学业上都是 minor 的直接对立面。

entries.definition: small in degree and often unimportant. It overlaps minor in the 'not serious' sense, but cannot carry the ranking or legal senses.
entries.definitionCN: 程度小，常不重要。它在“不严重”这一义项上与 minor 重叠，却不能承载等级或法律义。

normalIntro.en: Real grammar and real relatives: minor is already a Latin comparative, major is its opposite, minority and minimum share the same smallness root.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实语法与真实同族词：minor 本身就是拉丁比较级，major 是它的反面，minority 与 minimum 共享同一条“小”的词根。

normal.en: Minor is already a comparative in Latin, 'smaller'. English does not add -er to it, so there is no 'minorer'.
normal.cn: minor 在拉丁语里已经是比较级“更小的”。英语不再给它加 -er，所以不存在“minorer”这种形式。

normal.en: Major and minor are a pair: Latin maior and minor, both comparatives, one from magnus and one from the *mei- family.
normal.cn: major 与 minor 是一对：拉丁语 maior 与 minor 都是比较级，一个出自 magnus，一个出自 *mei- 词族。

normal.en: Minor key: the third is shorter than the major third, so the interval itself is literally minor.
normal.cn: 小调：它的三度比大三度短，所以这个音程本身就是“较小的”。

normal.en: A college minor is the smaller half of a double subject: fewer credits than the major.
normal.cn: 大学的辅修是双主修里较小的那一半：学分比主修少。

normal.en: Minor league teams sit below the major league; the word keeps the same 'lesser' ranking.
normal.cn: 小联盟球队坐在大联盟下面一级；这个词保留着同一个“次一等”的排名含义。

abstract.en: Picture a balance with two pans. Minor is not the pan that is empty; it is the pan that is lighter than the one opposite it.
abstract.cn: 想象一架有两只盘的天平。minor 不是空着的那只盘，而是比对面那只更轻的盘。

abstract.en: Minor does not mean tiny. It means smaller than the thing it is compared with, so a minor injury can still hurt.
abstract.cn: minor 不等于“极小”。它表示比对照物更小，所以轻伤也仍然会疼。

abstract.en: The same ranking word moves between size, importance, age and music: in each case something sits one step below its partner.
abstract.cn: 同一个表示排位的词在尺寸、重要性、年龄和音乐之间移动：每一种情形里，都有某物比它的伙伴低一级。

examples.en: The road was closed after a minor collision.
examples.cn: 一起小碰撞之后，这条路被封了。

examples.en: She majored in biology with a minor in statistics.
examples.cn: 她主修生物学，辅修统计学。

examples.en: The film's minor characters are more memorable than its hero.
examples.cn: 这部电影的次要角色比主角更令人难忘。

dict_mnemonic.text: “买呢”——买呢子大衣时只剩小一号的，只好买了那件小号的 → minor 较小的、次要的

root: 源自拉丁语 minor“更小的、更少的、更年幼的”，是 minus 一系的比较级，核心是“同一对里较轻的那一端”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of minor, all from one position: the lighter pan of a balance, the member of a pair that is smaller, lower, younger, or less important than its partner.
sensesIntro.cn: minor 的九个义项都来自同一个位置：天平上较轻的那只盘，也就是一对事物中比伙伴更小、更低、更年幼或更不重要的那一个。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the lighter pan of a balance, always weighed against a heavier partner.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平上较轻的那只盘，永远与更重的伙伴一起被衡量。

branches.en: SIZE AND DEGREE: the shorter of two paired things, or a degree too small to count as serious.
branches.cn: 尺寸与程度：一对事物中较短的那一个，或小到不算严重的程度。

branches.en: RANK: a lesser role in a negotiation, and the leagues that sit below the major ones.
branches.cn: 等级：谈判中较次要的角色，以及坐在大联盟下面一级的联赛。

branches.en: AGE: the adjective and the noun both mark a person below the legal line of full adult rights.
branches.cn: 年龄：形容词与名词都标记处于完整成年权利线以下的人。

branches.en: MUSIC: a third shorter than the major third gives the minor key its name.
branches.cn: 音乐：比大三度短的三度，给了小调这个名字。

branches.en: FORMAL SUBSYSTEMS: the minor premise and the secondary subject are each the lesser member of a pair.
branches.cn: 形式化的子系统：小前提与辅修科目，各自都是一对中的较小成员。

intro.en: Minor is not built with an English affix; it is a Latin comparative borrowed whole. Its family grows through -ity, through compounds such as minor league and minor key, and through the related *mei- root.
intro.cn: minor 不是用英语词缀构成的，而是整体借入的拉丁比较级。它的词族通过 -ity、通过 minor league 与 minor key 这类复合词，以及通过相关的 *mei- 词根扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin minor, minus and minimus belong to one scale: minor 'smaller', minus 'less', minimus 'smallest'. Parvus 'small' is traditionally paired with them in grammar, but it is a different root, so the relation is suppletive rather than derivational.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 minor、minus、minimus 属于同一把尺子：minor“更小”、minus“更少”、minimus“最小”。parvus“小”在语法传统上与它们配成一组，但它是另一条词根，因此这是异根补充关系，而不是派生关系。

items.structure: Latin minor, comparative of the *mei- family
items.meaningCN: 更小的；较次要的；较年幼的（拉丁语比较级）
items.example: The minor road joins the highway two miles north.
items.exampleCN: 那条小路在往北两英里处接入高速公路。

items.meaning: a smaller group; the state of being under age
items.meaningCN: 少数群体；未成年状态（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The proposal was supported by only a small minority.
items.exampleCN: 这项提案只得到一小部分人的支持。

items.meaning: a sports league below the top professional level
items.meaningCN: 低于顶级职业水平的体育联赛（复合名词）
items.example: He played five years in the minor leagues.

items.meaning: a musical key built on a minor third
items.meaningCN: 以小三级构成的小调（复合名词）
items.example: The scene is scored in a slow minor key.
items.exampleCN: 这一幕配的是缓慢的小调。

items.meaningCN: 最小量；最低限度（minimus 的中性形式）
items.example: Keep the temperature at a minimum of ten degrees.
items.exampleCN: 把温度保持在至少十度。

items.meaning: to reduce to the smallest amount
items.meaningCN: 使最小化；把……降到最低（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The new route minimizes travel time.
items.exampleCN: 新路线把行程时间减到最少。

items.meaning: less; the subtraction sign; a drawback
items.meaningCN: 减去；负号；不利因素（minor 的中性形式）
items.example: The plan has one clear minus: it is expensive.
items.exampleCN: 这个方案有一个明显的短板：它很贵。

items.meaningCN: 减少；削弱（di- 离开 + minuere 减少）
items.example: Interest in the case diminished over the years.
items.exampleCN: 这些年，人们对这桩案子的兴趣减弱了。

items.meaningCN: 极小的（作形容词，来自拉丁语 minutus“小的”）
items.example: The differences between the two samples are minute.
items.exampleCN: 两个样本之间的差异极其微小。

items.meaning: a person who serves in a government or church
items.meaningCN: 部长；大臣；牧师（拉丁语 minister“仆人”，源自 minus）
items.example: The foreign minister signed the agreement.
items.exampleCN: 外交部长签署了这项协议。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 更小的；较少的；较年幼的

latinEntries.structure: neuter of minor, used as a noun and preposition

definition_zh: 少数；少数派；少数群体；少数民族；未成年
definition_en: the smaller number or part of a group, a group that differs from most people, or the state of being below the legal age
core_image: 一大群白鸟里混着几只深色的鸟，深色的那几只格外显眼
scene: 礼堂里举手表决时，只有靠后排的几个人没有举手，显得有些孤单。A minority of members opposed the plan.
sceneCN: 这里 minority 是「少数、少数票」（第 1 个义项：人数较少的那一部分）；句意为少数成员反对这项计划。画面里可抓住的物件：礼堂、举起的手、后排的几个人。

pos.zh: 少数；少数派；少数群体；少数民族；未成年

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁比较级 minor 直接借入，义为「较小的；次要的；未成年的」
由 minority 词干加 -arian 构成，义为「少数派的；少数派成员」
由 minority 与 owned 复合，义为「少数族裔拥有的」

senses.title: The smaller number in a group
senses.definition: the smaller part of a group, less than half of the people involved
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体中人数较少的那一部分，即不到参与人数的一半
senses.example: Only a minority of shareholders backed the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 只有少数股东支持这次合并。
senses.why: The word is built on Latin minor, smaller, so the first sense simply compares two parts of a vote or a crowd and names the smaller one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语 minor（较小的）之上，所以第一个义项只是把投票或人群分成两份，取其中较小的那一份。

senses.title: A group that differs from most people
senses.definition: a group of people who differ from the larger society in race, religion, language or culture
senses.definitionCN: 在种族、宗教、语言或文化上与更大的社会群体不同的一群人
senses.example: The school teaches in the languages of several minorities.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校用几种少数民族的语言授课。
senses.why: Once the smaller part is made of people with a shared identity, the comparative word becomes a social label for communities outside the majority.
senses.whyCN: 当那较小的一部分是由具有共同身份的人组成时，这个比较词就变成社会标签，用来指多数群体之外的社群。

senses.title: The state of being under legal age
senses.definition: the period during which a person is legally too young to manage their own affairs
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在法定上年纪尚小、不能自行处理事务的那段时期
senses.example: He inherited the estate while still in his minority.
senses.exampleCN: 他还在未成年时便继承了这份产业。
senses.why: Latin minor also meant younger, and the law borrowed the comparison to mark who is less than the age of full legal capacity.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 minor 也有「较年轻」的意思，法律借用了这个比较，用来标出未达到完全法定年龄的人。

intro.en: Minority comes from Latin minor, smaller or younger, and reached English through French; its senses follow both comparisons, the smaller part and the younger person.
intro.cn: minority 来自拉丁语 minor（较小的、较年轻的），经法语进入英语；它的义项沿着两种比较展开：较少的部分与较年轻的人。

items.en: Minor was the comparative of parvus, meaning smaller, lesser or younger, and it is the stem behind the whole family.
items.cn: minor 是 parvus 的比较级，意为较小、较低或较年轻，是整族词的词干。

items.en: The abstract noun minoritas was formed with -itas to name the state of being smaller or younger.
items.cn: 抽象名词 minoritas 由 -itas 构成，用来指「较小」或「较年轻」的状态。

items.en: French used minorité for both the smaller part and the years before adulthood, and this form generally reached English.
items.cn: 法语用 minorité 兼指较少的部分与成年之前的年月，一般认为英语接收的正是这个形式。

items.en: English minority first named the state of being under age, and the sense of a smaller number followed.
items.cn: 英语中 minority 最早指未成年的状态，随后才出现「人数较少」的义项。

items.en: Modern English keeps both senses and adds the social sense of an ethnic or religious minority.
items.cn: 现代英语保留这两个义项，并增加了「民族或宗教上的少数群体」这一社会义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin comparison of small; the near-meaning group collects words for a small part, a faction and the years before adulthood.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁「小」的比较系列上的词；近义组收表示小部分、派系与成年之前年岁的词。

entries.definition: Smaller, less important, or below the legal age of adulthood.
entries.definitionCN: 较小的、较次要的，或未达法定成年年龄的。

entries.definition: The mathematical sign for subtraction, or a state of being without something.
entries.definitionCN: 数学中的减号，或缺少某物的状态。

entries.definition: To become smaller or less in size, amount or importance.
entries.definitionCN: 在大小、数量或重要性上变小或减少。

entries.definition: As small as possible; at the lowest end of a scale.
entries.definitionCN: 尽可能小的；处在标度最低端的。

entries.definition: A very small number of people or things.
entries.definitionCN: 为数极少的人或物。

entries.definition: A small part of a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 整体中很小的一部分。

entries.definition: A small organized group within a larger one, often in disagreement with it.
entries.definitionCN: 较大团体内部一个有组织的小派别，常与主体意见不合。

entries.definition: Below the age at which the law treats a person as an adult.
entries.definitionCN: 低于法律视为成年人的年龄。

normalIntro.en: Minority is the state built on Latin minor, smaller or younger, and its family keeps measuring things against a larger other side.
normalIntro.cn: minority 建立在拉丁语 minor（较小、较年轻）之上的状态，它的一族词始终拿「更大的另一边」作参照。

normal.en: Minority is built on minor, Latin for smaller or younger, so the word carries a comparison before it carries any social meaning.
normal.cn: minority 建立在 minor（较小或较年轻）之上，所以这个词先带比较，再带社会含义。

normal.en: The -ity ending turns an adjective into a state or condition, just as major becomes majority.
normal.cn: -ity 词尾把形容词变成状态或性质，就像 major 变成 majority 一样。

normal.en: In the minority is the everyday frame: whoever is counted there is on the smaller side of a vote.
normal.cn: in the minority 是日常框架：被算在里面的人，就是投票中人数较少的一边。

normal.en: Ethnic minority and minority group show the word naming communities, not just numbers.
normal.cn: ethnic minority 与 minority group 展示了这个词如何命名社群，而不只是数字。

normal.en: The legal sense is the older one in English: minority first meant the years before a person reaches full age.
normal.cn: 法律义在英语里更早：minority 最初指一个人达到完全年龄之前的那些年。

abstract.en: Picture a flock of pale birds with a few darker ones among them: the dark birds are few but easy to see.
abstract.cn: 想象一大群浅色鸟里夹着几只深色的：深色的数量少，却很容易被看见。

abstract.en: A minority is a comparison turned into a group; the word always implies a larger other side.
abstract.cn: minority 是被变成群体的比较；这个词始终暗示着一个更大的对立面。

abstract.en: The same stem covers a voting count, a community and a child's years, because all three are measured as less than something else.
abstract.cn: 同一个词干覆盖投票计数、社群与童年，因为三者都是相对于某个更大对象而被量出来的「较少」。

examples.en: Only a minority of shareholders backed the merger.
examples.cn: 只有少数股东支持这次合并。

examples.en: The school teaches in the languages of several minorities.
examples.cn: 这所学校用几种少数民族的语言授课。

examples.en: He inherited the estate while still in his minority.
examples.cn: 他还在未成年时便继承了这份产业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买诺瑞提」——买票时数一数，多数一大把，少数就那么几张，提出来格外显眼；minority 是少数。

root: 拉丁语 minor（较小的、较年轻的）是 parvus（小）的比较级；抽象名词 minoritas 经法语 minorité 进入英语，一般认为先指未成年，后指少数。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the smaller side of a comparison; the senses run from a voting count to a social group and to the years before legal adulthood.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是比较中较小的那一边；各义项从投票计数走到社会群体，再到法定成年之前的年岁。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flock of pale birds with a few darker ones standing out among them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一大群浅色鸟里，几只深色的格外显眼。

branches.en: a few hands raised against a crowded hall
branches.cn: 满堂之中只有几只举起的手

branches.en: a classroom where several home languages are spoken
branches.cn: 几种家庭语言同时存在的教室

branches.en: a young heir signing papers before coming of age
branches.cn: 未成年的继承人签下文件

branches.en: a small group that shares a name and a voice
branches.cn: 人数少却有共同名字与声音的一群人

branches.en: the same word measuring a community and a childhood
branches.cn: 同一个词既量社群也量童年

intro.en: Minority joins a Latin comparative of small to an abstract suffix, and its items show how a comparison becomes a social category.
intro.cn: minority 把拉丁语「小」的比较级接到抽象后缀上，各构词条目展示了比较如何变成社会类别。

latinIntro.en: Minority rests on the Latin comparative minor, smaller or younger, and the same stem appears in minor, minus and diminish.
latinIntro.cn: minority 建立在拉丁语比较级 minor（较小的、较年轻的）之上，同一词干见于 minor、minus 与 diminish。

definition_zh: 分钟；片刻；会议记录；极小的；细微的
definition_en: a unit of time equal to sixty seconds; a short moment; the written record of a meeting; and, with a different pronunciation, extremely small or very detailed
core_image: 桌上小钟的秒针走完一圈，一小时被切成六十个小格
scene: 会议室门口，秘书把一叠记录纸递过来说人已到齐，主席却还在楼梯上。The chair opened the meeting a minute late.
sceneCN: 这里是「分钟」（第 1 个义项：时间单位）；句意为主席晚了很短的时间才宣布开会。图中可辨识物件：记录纸、会议室门牌、秒针。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词 minute 加 -ly 构成，义为「细微地；精确地」，读作长音
由形容词 minute 加 -ness 构成，义为「微小；精细」
拉丁语 minutia 的复数，与 minute 同出 minutus（变小），义为「细枝末节」

senses.title: A unit of sixty seconds
senses.definition: a period of time equal to sixty seconds, one sixtieth of an hour
senses.definitionCN: 等于六十秒的一段时间，即一小时的六十分之一
senses.example: The film runs ninety minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片放映九十分钟。
senses.why: Latin named this unit pars minuta prima, the first small part of an hour, and the adjective minutus, made small, is the part English kept as the name of the unit.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语把这个单位叫作 pars minuta prima，即「一小时的第一小部分」，其中表示「变小」的形容词 minutus 被英语保留下来，成了这个时间单位的名字。

senses.title: A short, indefinite stretch of time
senses.definition: a very short period of time, often used loosely rather than as exactly sixty seconds
senses.definitionCN: 极短的一段时间，常是模糊的说法，而不是精确的六十秒
senses.example: Wait a minute, I left the keys inside.
senses.exampleCN: 等一下，我把钥匙落在里面了。
senses.why: Once a minute names a small division of the hour, it can stand for any brief interval, because the word has already been marked as small.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 minute 指小时里的一小格，它就能代表任何短暂的间隔，因为这个词本身已经被标记成「小」。

senses.title: Extremely small in size
senses.definition: extremely small, so small that it is easy to overlook
senses.definitionCN: 极其小，小到容易被忽略
senses.example: The cracks in the glass were minute and hard to see.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃上的裂纹极小，很难看清。
senses.why: The adjective came straight from Latin minutus, made small, and it kept the literal sense of size while the noun moved off to the clock; English also gives it a long vowel, which is why the two senses sound different.
senses.whyCN: 形容词直接来自拉丁语 minutus（变小），保留了字面上的尺寸义，而名词则走去指钟表上的单位；英语还让形容词读长音，所以两种义项听起来不同。

senses.title: Very detailed and precise
senses.definition: done with close attention to small details, as in a minute account or a minute examination
senses.definitionCN: 对细小之处极为留意的，如细致的叙述或细致的检查
senses.example: The report gives a minute account of the experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告对实验作了极为细致的记述。
senses.why: If something is so small that it needs a close look, then a close look is what the adjective also describes, so from tiny size the word slides to care about tiny detail.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物小到必须凑近才看得清，那么这种凑近的查看本身也能被同一个形容词描述，于是词义从「尺寸极小」滑向「对细处极用心」。

senses.title: The official record of a meeting
senses.definition: the written notes of what was said and decided at a meeting, usually kept in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 会议上发言与决定的书面记录，通常用复数
senses.example: The secretary took the minutes in shorthand.
senses.exampleCN: 秘书用速记做会议记录。
senses.why: Early clerks wrote the record of a meeting in very small script to save paper, and the Latin word for small gave both the script and the record its name, which is why the notes are minutes.
senses.whyCN: 早期文书为了省纸，把会议记录写得很小，拉丁语中表示「小」的词同时给了这种小字和记录本身一个名字，所以记录叫 minutes。

intro.en: Minute carries two histories in one spelling: a Latin adjective meaning made small gave both the clock unit and the adjective, and English separated them by pronunciation.
intro.cn: minute 一个拼写里装着两段历史：拉丁语中表示「变小」的形容词既生出钟表单位，也生出形容词，英语用读音把它们分开了。

items.en: Minutus meant made small, a participle of the verb minuere, to lessen, and it described anything reduced in size.
items.cn: minutus 意为「被弄小的」，是动词 minuere（减少）的分词，用来描述任何被缩小的东西。

items.en: The phrase pars minuta prima, first small part, named one sixtieth of an hour and one sixtieth of a degree, and the small-part word was carried into the unit.
items.cn: 短语 pars minuta prima 意为「第一小部分」，指一小时的六十分之一与一度的六十分之一，这个「小部分」的词后来进入了单位名称。

items.en: Old French used minute for a small written note, especially the clerk's draft of a legal or official record.
items.cn: 古法语用 minute 指小字写的便条，尤指文书对法律或公务记录的草稿。

items.en: Middle English minute named both the sixtieth of an hour and a brief moment, while the adjective small sense entered from written Latin.
items.cn: 中古英语的 minute 既指一小时的六十分之一，也指短暂的片刻；表示「小」的形容词义则从书面拉丁语进入。

items.en: Modern English keeps the noun with a short vowel, the adjective with a long vowel, and the plural minutes for the record of a meeting.
items.cn: 现代英语让名词读短音、形容词读长音，并用复数 minutes 指会议记录。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin root of smallness through derived adverbs and nouns; the near-meaning group gathers other words for short stretches of time.
note.cn: 形近组顺着表示「小」的拉丁词根，收派生副词与名词；近义组收其他表示短暂时间的词。

entries.definition: In tiny detail; with close attention to small parts.
entries.definitionCN: 以极细的程度；对细部极为留意地。

entries.definition: The quality of being extremely small.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的性质。

entries.definition: Extremely small, or a word form marking smallness.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的；指小的词形。

entries.definition: The Latin verb meaning to lessen, listed here for the root only.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语动词「减少」，此处仅列词根。

entries.definition: A very short period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 极短的一段时间。

entries.definition: A unit of time equal to one sixtieth of a minute.
entries.definitionCN: 等于一分钟六十分之一的时间单位。

entries.definition: A single point in time, or a very brief moment.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时刻；极短的瞬间。

entries.definition: A period of time, usually short and vague.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间，通常短暂而模糊。

normalIntro.en: One Latin adjective for small feeds two separate words, so the family splits between clock time, tiny size and the paper record of a meeting.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「小」的拉丁形容词喂出两条不同的词路，词族因此分到钟表时间、极小尺寸与会议纸面记录。

normal.en: The time unit began as pars minuta prima, the first small part of an hour, so minute literally names a small slice of time.
normal.cn: 这个时间单位起初是 pars minuta prima，即「一小时的第一小部分」，所以 minute 字面上就是时间的一小片。

normal.en: The adjective keeps the Latin sense of minutus, made small, and English marks it with a long vowel so the ear can tell it from the clock word.
normal.cn: 形容词保留了拉丁语 minutus（变小）的意思，英语用长音标记它，让耳朵能把它与钟表那个词分开。

normal.en: Minutes of a meeting were first notes written in small script, which is why the official record shares the spelling of the small adjective.
normal.cn: 会议记录最初是用小字写下的笔记，所以正式记录与小这个形容词共用同一个拼写。

normal.en: Minutely and minuteness belong to the small adjective rather than to the time noun, and their vowels show which branch they come from.
normal.cn: minutely 与 minuteness 属于「小」的形容词，而不是时间名词，它们的元音显示了自己来自哪一支。

normal.en: Diminutive comes from the same Latin verb minuere, to lessen, so the whole family keeps returning to shrinking.
normal.cn: diminutive 出自同一个拉丁动词 minuere（减少），整个词族不断回到「缩小」这个动作。

abstract.en: Picture a clock face cut into sixty thin slices, then one slice held up close enough to show its scratches.
abstract.cn: 想象钟面被切成六十片薄片，然后取一片凑近到能看清上面的划痕。

abstract.en: The same word measures the hour and the speck of dust: smallness is the thread joining the clock to the microscope.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既量一小时，也量一粒尘：小是把钟表与显微镜串起来的那根线。

abstract.en: A meeting becomes a few written pages, and those pages are named after the smallness of the handwriting that saved paper.
abstract.cn: 一场会议变成几页纸，而这几页纸得名于当初为省纸而写的小字。

examples.en: The train leaves in a minute.
examples.cn: 列车一分钟后开。

examples.en: The letters on the coin were minute and hard to read.
examples.cn: 硬币上的字母极小，很难辨认。

examples.en: She took the minutes at every board meeting.
examples.cn: 每次董事会都由她做记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迷你特」——迷你的本子很小，翻一页只花一分钟；记住 minute 既指分钟，也指微小的。

root: 拉丁语 minutus（变小，出自 minuere「减少」）；时间义来自 pars minuta prima（一小时的第一小部分），形容词义直接来自 minutus；会议记录义经古法语 minute（小字记录）进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small piece of the hour; the senses divide into the clock unit, the vague short moment, the tiny size kept by the adjective, the close detail that size demands, and the small-script record of a meeting.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「小时里的一小片」；义项分到钟表单位、模糊的短暂片刻、形容词保留的极小尺寸、小尺寸所要求的细致，以及用小字写成的会议记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small clock hand sweeping a circle cut into sixty narrow slices.
core.cn: 核心意象：小小的钟表指针扫过被切成六十个窄格的圆盘。

branches.en: a clock face divided into sixty slices
branches.cn: 钟面被分成六十格

branches.en: someone holding a door and saying just a moment
branches.cn: 有人扶住门说再等一下

branches.en: a crack too thin for the eye to catch
branches.cn: 细得眼睛看不见的裂纹

branches.en: a page of notes on the smallest parts of a test
branches.cn: 一页记着实验最细处的笔记

branches.en: a clerk writing the meeting in tiny script
branches.cn: 文书用小字记下会议

intro.en: Latin words for small and to lessen supply the stem, and English suffixes build the adverb, the quality noun and the family word for a small form.
intro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「小」与「减少」的词提供词干，英语后缀则造出副词、性质名词，以及与「指小」相关的词族成员。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 镜子；镜面；写照；反映；映照
definition_en: a piece of glass with a reflective coating that shows images; also something that gives a faithful picture of a situation, and to show or match something as a mirror does
core_image: 晨光里的一面镜子，把窗前的人原样照回来
scene: 清晨的走廊上，她把外套领子翻正，又抬手理了理头发。She checked her collar in the mirror before the interview.
sceneCN: 这里是「镜子」（第 1 个义项：能照出影像的玻璃物件）；句意为面试前她对着镜子整理衣领。图中可辨识物件：镜子、衣领、走廊灯。

derivatives.zh: 由动词 mirror 加 -ing 构成，义为「镜像；反映」
由动词 mirror 加 -ed 构成，义为「装有镜子的；映出的」
由 mirror 加表示「没有」的 -less 构成，义为「无镜的」，多指相机结构

senses.title: A glass surface that shows a reflection
senses.definition: a piece of glass or polished surface with a reflective coating that shows the image of what stands before it
senses.definitionCN: 镀有反光层的玻璃或抛光表面，能照出面前事物的影像
senses.example: She checked her collar in the mirror before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前她对着镜子整理衣领。
senses.why: The word came through Old French from a Vulgar Latin noun for a looking glass, built on the verb mirari, to look at or wonder at, so the object is named for the gaze it invites.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经古法语来自一个表示「照人用的玻璃」的俗拉丁名词，后者建于动词 mirari（注视、惊叹）之上，所以物件是按它招来的那道目光命名的。

senses.title: A faithful picture of a situation
senses.definition: a person or thing that shows a situation, a period or a mood exactly as it is
senses.definitionCN: 把某种局面、时代或情绪如实呈现出来的人或事物
senses.example: The novel is a mirror of its age.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说是那个时代的写照。
senses.why: Because a mirror returns an exact image rather than a flattering one, writers use it for anything that shows a situation without distortion, and a novel can serve as that surface.
senses.whyCN: 镜子给出的是准确而非讨好的影像，作家便用它指任何不失真地呈现局面的东西，一部小说也能充当这样一面镜面。

senses.title: To show an image as a mirror does
senses.definition: to show the image of something, the way a still surface reflects what stands beside it
senses.definitionCN: 像平静表面那样把旁边的事物影像呈现出来
senses.example: The lake mirrored the pines along the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 湖面映出岸边的松树。
senses.why: The verb was simply the noun turned into an action, so to mirror is to do what a mirror does: send back the image of whatever stands before it.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词就是把名词直接变成动作，所以 to mirror 就是做镜子所做的事：把面前事物的影像送回原处。

senses.title: To match or correspond closely
senses.definition: to be very similar to something else, so that the two seem to copy each other
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物极为相似，看上去像彼此复制出来的一样
senses.example: The vote mirrored the national trend.
senses.exampleCN: 投票结果与全国趋势一致。
senses.why: When two patterns look identical, one seems to be the reflection of the other, so the verb widened from reflecting light to reflecting behaviour, numbers and opinions.
senses.whyCN: 当两种走势看起来一模一样，其中一个就像是另一个的倒影，于是这个动词从映出光线扩展到映出行为、数字与观点。

intro.en: Mirror comes from a Vulgar Latin name for a looking glass, built on the verb mirari, to look at or wonder at, and it reached English through Old French.
intro.cn: mirror 来自俗拉丁语中「照人用的玻璃」这一名称，建立在动词 mirari（注视、惊叹）之上，再经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Mirari meant to look at with wonder, and the looking and the wondering were not separated in the verb.
items.cn: mirari 意为带着惊叹地看，在这个动词里，「看」与「惊叹」并没有分开。

items.en: A Vulgar Latin noun, reconstructed as miratorium, named the thing one looks into; the form is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 俗拉丁语中有一个表示「供人照看的器物」的名词，学界重构为 miratorium；这是重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: Old French mirour carried the noun into ordinary use for the polished metal or glass a person looks into.
items.cn: 古法语 mirour 把这个名词带入日常用法，指人们照看的抛光金属或玻璃。

items.en: Middle English mirrour kept the extra vowel of the French form and also used the word for moral examples and ideal portraits.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mirrour 保留了法语形式里多出的元音，也用这个词指道德榜样与理想化的画像。

items.en: Modern English shortened the spelling to mirror, formed a matching verb, and pushed the word into talk about trends, reports and behaviour.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写缩成 mirror，造出与之相配的动词，并把这个词推进到关于趋势、报告与行为的说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb for looking and wondering; the near-meaning group gathers words for reflections and for the surfaces that produce them.
note.cn: 形近组顺着拉丁语中表示「看」与「惊叹」的动词展开；近义组收表示影像以及产生影像的表面的词。

entries.definition: An optical illusion in which water seems to appear in the distance.
entries.definitionCN: 远处看似有水的一种光学幻景。

entries.definition: To look at someone with wonder and approval.
entries.definitionCN: 带着惊叹与赞许地看某人。

entries.definition: An astonishing event believed to come from divine power.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为是神力所致的惊人之事。

entries.definition: The act of reflecting an image, or of copying another's behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 映出影像的行为，或模仿他人行为的过程。

entries.definition: The image of something seen in a mirror or on water.
entries.definitionCN: 镜中或水面看到的事物的影像。

entries.definition: A hard, transparent material, or a mirror made from it.
entries.definitionCN: 坚硬透明的材料，或用它制成的镜子。

entries.definition: A picture or likeness of someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 某人某物的图像或相似物。

entries.definition: To send back light or an image, or to show a situation.
entries.definitionCN: 把光或影像送回；反映某种情况。

normalIntro.en: The Latin verb for looking and wondering gives the noun, and the noun then turns into a verb, so the family keeps moving between the glass and the act of copying.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「看」与「惊叹」的动词生出名词，名词又变成动词，于是词族在镜面与复制这个动作之间来回移动。

normal.en: Mirari means to look at with wonder, and a mirror was first a looking glass, so the object is named for the gaze it invites.
normal.cn: mirari 意为带着惊叹地看，而 mirror 起初就是照人的玻璃，所以这个物件按它招来的目光得名。

normal.en: Mirror, miracle, mirage and admire share that Latin verb, which is why looking and wondering sit close together in this family.
normal.cn: mirror、miracle、mirage 与 admire 共用那个拉丁动词，所以看与惊叹在这个词族里挨得很近。

normal.en: The noun came first, and to mirror is a later verb made by simply treating the object as an action.
normal.cn: 名词先出现，to mirror 是后来把这个物件直接当作动作来用才有的动词。

normal.en: Mirror image names a copy reversed left to right, the most literal use of the noun in front of another noun.
normal.cn: mirror image 指左右颠倒的复制影像，是名词放在另一个名词前最字面的用法。

normal.en: The phrase a mirror of the times still demands a faithful picture, not a flattering one.
normal.cn: a mirror of the times 这一说法仍然要求如实呈现，而不是美化。

abstract.en: Picture a still lake at dawn returning the trees exactly, without adding or hiding anything.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明时平静的湖面把树影原样送回，既不增添也不隐藏。

abstract.en: A mirror can flatter or accuse, but it cannot lie about the shape in front of it; the word keeps that demand for accuracy.
abstract.cn: 镜子可以讨好也可以揭短，但它无法对面前的形状说谎；这个词一直保留着这份准确的要求。

abstract.en: To mirror someone is to become their reflection, which is why imitation and understanding can look the same from outside.
abstract.cn: to mirror 某人就是成为他的倒影，所以模仿与理解从外面看往往一模一样。

examples.en: She checked her collar in the mirror.
examples.cn: 她对着镜子整理衣领。

examples.en: The lake mirrored the pines along the shore.
examples.cn: 湖面映出岸边的松树。

examples.en: The report mirrors what workers have been saying for years.
examples.cn: 这份报告反映了工人们多年来的说法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米勒」——米勒站在镜前，镜里镜外一个样；记住 mirror 是镜子，也指反映。

root: 俗拉丁语 miratorium（照人的器物，重构形式）出自拉丁语 mirari（注视、惊叹），经古法语 mirour 与中古英语 mirrour 进入现代英语；与 miracle、mirage、admire 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a surface that returns an image; the senses divide into the glass itself, the faithful picture it stands for, the act of sending back an image, and the matching of two patterns.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把影像送回原处的表面」；义项分到玻璃物件本身、它所代表的如实写照、送回影像的动作，以及两种走势的彼此吻合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mirror in morning light returning the person in front of it unchanged.
core.cn: 核心意象：晨光中的一面镜子，把镜前的人原样送回。

branches.en: a hall stand with a coat and a mirror
branches.cn: 门厅里挂着外套的镜子

branches.en: a novel read as a portrait of its decade
branches.cn: 一部被当作时代画像来读的小说

branches.en: pines repeated on still water
branches.cn: 静水里重复出现的松树

branches.en: two line graphs rising in the same shape
branches.cn: 两条走势完全相同的折线

branches.en: a faithful image and a matching pattern share one verb
branches.cn: 如实的写照与吻合的走势共用一个动词

intro.en: A reconstructed Vulgar Latin noun and the Latin verb for wondering supply the stem, and English suffixes build the adjective, the action noun and the negative form.
intro.cn: 一个重构的俗拉丁名词与表示「惊叹」的拉丁动词提供词干，英语后缀则造出形容词、动作名词与否定义的形式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。
