definition_zh: 痛苦；苦难；不幸的事；（口语）总在抱怨的人
definition_en: great unhappiness or suffering, especially when it lasts a long time; a cause or source of hardship; and, informally, a person who complains constantly
core_image: 冷屋子的角落里，一个人把旧毯子拉到下巴，窗外雨声不停
scene: 屋子里没有生火，雨点一直敲着窗，一个人蜷在角落，把旧毯子拉到下巴。Years of misery had worn the family down before help arrived.
sceneCN: 这里是「痛苦、苦难」（第 1 个义项：长期的痛苦处境）；句意为在援助到来之前，多年的苦难已经把这一家人拖垮了。图中可辨识物件：没有生火的屋子、敲窗的雨、拉到下巴的旧毯子。

pos.zh: 痛苦；苦难；不幸的事；总在抱怨的人

collocations.phrase: put someone out of their misery
collocations.zh: 结束某人的痛苦；让某人不必再猜

derivatives.zh: 与 misery 同出拉丁语 miser，义为「痛苦的；悲惨的」
由拉丁语 miser 经英语演变而来，义为「吝啬的」
由 com- 与拉丁语 miserari 构成，义为「同情；慰问」

senses.title: Great unhappiness or suffering
senses.definition: a state of deep unhappiness and pain, especially one that lasts over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 深深的痛苦与难受，尤指持续很久的状态
senses.example: Years of misery had worn the family down before help arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 在援助到来之前，多年的苦难已经把这一家人拖垮了。
senses.why: Latin miseria named wretchedness as a condition, so misery begins as a place a person is stuck in rather than as a mood that passes through.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 miseria 把悲惨说成一种处境，所以 misery 起初是一个人被困住的地方，而不是一阵会过去的心情。

senses.title: A cause or source of hardship
senses.definition: something such as poverty, illness or loss that brings suffering to people
senses.definitionCN: 贫穷、疾病或丧失之类给人带来痛苦的事
senses.example: The flood brought misery to hundreds of villages.
senses.exampleCN: 那场洪水给数百个村庄带来了苦难。
senses.why: Once miseria names the condition, the things that produce it can take the same word, because English often lets a cause borrow the name of its effect.
senses.whyCN: miseria 一旦指这种处境，制造这种处境的事物也能用同一个词，因为英语常让原因借用结果的名字。

senses.title: A person who complains all the time
senses.definition: in informal British use, someone who is habitually gloomy and complains about everything
senses.definitionCN: 英国口语用法，指一贯阴郁、对什么都抱怨的人
senses.example: Don't be such a misery and come to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 别这么爱抱怨了，来参加聚会吧。
senses.why: The word moves from the feeling to the person who carries it into a room; a misery is someone whose company spreads the very state the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从感受转到把感受带进房间的人；一个 misery 就是那种一在场就把这种状态扩散开来的人。

intro.en: Misery comes from Latin miseria, the noun for wretchedness built on miser, and it reached English by way of Old French.
intro.cn: misery 来自拉丁语 miseria，即建立在 miser 之上、表示悲惨处境的名称，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Miseria named wretchedness, hardship and distress, and it was formed directly on miser, the word for a wretched person.
items.cn: miseria 意为悲惨、困苦、痛苦，直接由表示可怜人的 miser 构成。

items.en: Miser described someone unhappy, pitiable or living in bad circumstances, and it supplied the root for the whole family.
items.cn: miser 形容一个人不快乐、可怜或境遇糟糕，为整个词族提供了词根。

items.en: Old French took miseria as misere, meaning distress and hardship, and passed it on to English.
items.cn: 古法语把 miseria 写作 misere，意为痛苦与困苦，并把它传给英语。

items.en: Middle English misery covered both the state of suffering and the events that caused it.
items.cn: 中古英语的 misery 既指受苦的状态，也指造成痛苦的事件。

items.en: Modern English kept the serious sense and added an informal one for a person who complains without end.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了严肃的义项，又增加了一个口语义，指没完没了抱怨的人。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Latin miser and two neighbours that only share its shape; the near-meaning group collects words for suffering and for deep sorrow.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一个拉丁词 miser 上的词，以及两个只在字形上相近的词；近义组收表示受苦与深切悲伤的词。

entries.definition: Very unhappy, or very bad in condition.
entries.definitionCN: 非常不快乐，或境况极差。

entries.definition: To express sympathy for someone's misfortune.
entries.definitionCN: 对别人的不幸表示同情。

entries.definition: An economic measure that adds unemployment and inflation rates.
entries.definitionCN: 把失业率与通胀率相加的一种经济指标。

entries.definition: Unwilling to spend money; it shares the Latin root but took the sense of a hoarder.
entries.definitionCN: 不愿花钱的；与 miser 同根，但取了「囤积者」那一层意思。

entries.definition: The experience of pain, illness or hardship.
entries.definitionCN: 疼痛、疾病或困苦的经历。

entries.definition: Very severe mental or physical pain.
entries.definitionCN: 极严重的精神或肉体痛苦。

entries.definition: Extreme worry, sadness or discomfort.
entries.definitionCN: 极度的忧虑、悲伤或不适。

entries.definition: Great sorrow or the trouble that causes it.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的悲伤，或造成悲伤的祸患。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun for wretchedness; its family keeps returning to the state of suffering, the events that cause it, and the people who carry it into a room.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示悲惨处境的拉丁语名词上，同族词反复回到受苦的状态、造成痛苦的事件，以及把痛苦带进房间的人。

normal.en: Miseria is Latin for wretchedness, and it was built on miser, the word for a wretched person.
normal.cn: miseria 是拉丁语中表示悲惨的词，建立在表示可怜人的 miser 上。

normal.en: Misery keeps the same root as miserable, but the noun names the state while the adjective names the person or thing inside it.
normal.cn: misery 与 miserable 同根，但名词指状态，形容词指处在状态里的人或物。

normal.en: The plural miseries names specific hardships, because a long state of suffering is usually made of many separate blows.
normal.cn: 复数 miseries 指一桩桩具体的不幸，因为长期的受苦通常由许多次打击组成。

normal.en: The phrase 「put someone out of their misery」 first meant to end a creature's suffering, and it now also means to end someone's suspense.
normal.cn: 「put someone out of their misery」起初指结束一个生灵的痛苦，现在也指让某人不必再猜。

normal.en: 「Misery loves company」 is an old saying that treats sorrow as something looking for other people to sit beside.
normal.cn: 「misery loves company」是一句老话，把悲伤看成会去找别人来陪坐的东西。

abstract.en: A cold room with a dying lamp is misery as a place a person cannot leave, not as a mood that passes.
abstract.cn: 一间冷屋子加上一盏将灭的灯，就是 misery：它是人离不开的地方，而不是会过去的心情。

abstract.en: Because the noun names both the feeling and its causes, a flood, a debt and a long illness can all be called miseries.
abstract.cn: 因为这个名词既指感受也指成因，一场洪水、一笔债和一场久病都能叫 miseries。

abstract.en: Calling a complainer a misery suggests that sorrow can spread from one person into a whole room.
abstract.cn: 把一个抱怨者叫作 misery，说明悲伤能从一个人扩散到整个房间。

examples.en: Years of misery had worn the family down before help arrived.
examples.cn: 在援助到来之前，多年的苦难已经把这一家人拖垮了。

examples.en: The flood brought misery to hundreds of villages.
examples.cn: 那场洪水给数百个村庄带来了苦难。

examples.en: Don't be such a misery and come to the party.
examples.cn: 别这么爱抱怨了，来参加聚会吧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米泽瑞」——米不够、灯又快灭，日子就苦；记住 misery 是痛苦、苦难。

root: 拉丁语 miser（不幸的人）派生 miseria（悲惨、苦难），经古法语 misere 进入英语；与 miserable、commiserate 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a stuck state of wretchedness; the senses divide into the lasting feeling, the events that cause it, and the person who spreads it through complaint.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一种无法摆脱的悲惨处境；义项分为持续的感受、造成感受的事件，以及靠抱怨把这种状态扩散开来的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corner in an unheated room, a figure wrapped in an old blanket, rain knocking on the window without stopping.
core.cn: 核心意象：冷屋子的角落里，一个人裹着旧毯子，窗外的雨敲个不停。

branches.en: a figure curled in a cold corner
branches.cn: 蜷在冷屋子角落里的人

branches.en: a flood taking away what a family had
branches.cn: 洪水冲走一个家庭原有的东西

branches.en: a debt that grows while a wage stays small
branches.cn: 工资不涨而债越滚越大

branches.en: a voice complaining through a whole meal
branches.cn: 一顿饭里抱怨不停的声音

branches.en: one gloomy guest darkening a bright room
branches.cn: 一个阴郁的客人让明亮的房间暗下来

intro.en: The word is carried by the Latin noun for wretchedness, the adjective behind it, the verb of pity, the French form and the English plural.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示悲惨处境的拉丁语名词、它背后的形容词、表示怜悯的动词、法语形式以及英语复数共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Misery comes from a Latin noun of wretchedness built on miser, so the Latin side records the noun, the adjective and the verb of pity.
latinIntro.cn: misery 来自建立在 miser 上、表示悲惨处境的拉丁语名词，因此拉丁同源部分记录名词、形容词与表示怜悯的动词。
